basis: First reader review after the edit stage (edit pass_seq 1). sync 04 run first (written=0, unchanged=8). Read in full: 1-fast.md, 2-deep.md, 3-do.md, 4-say.md, 5-quiz.md, sources.md (head), data/04-organizations/{cards,questions via 5-quiz,speak,tasks}.json, STARTUP.md entry for 04, the exemplar README. findings.section: A Control Tower landing zone applies preventive and detective controls to registered OUs (Exam trap)
findings.quote: > **Exam trap:** New accounts created outside Account Factory [are not bound by the registered OU's controls] until you [separately register the OU or enroll the account].
findings.evidence: Fact control-tower-preventive-apply-unenrolled-detective-enrolled-only: 'preventive controls apply to all member accounts under the OU, enrolled and unenrolled.' Fact control-tower-auto-enrollment-baseline-from-destination-ou: 'The account automatically receives baseline resources and control configurations from the destination organizational unit (OU) in AWS Control Tower.' The trap callout (skim-visible) says an account outside Account Factory gets none of the registered OU's controls; the Go deeper five lines below says the preventive controls (the SCPs) do reach it. She keeps the callout, not the Go deeper, and will answer 'the SCP does not apply' for an account created with CreateAccount and moved into a registered OU. Fix: scope the trap to what is true in every case: 'An account in an OU that is not registered, or an account that is not enrolled, gets no detective controls. Preventive controls reach every account under a registered OU.' Keep the AWS sentence in the Go deeper with that explanation.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): 2-deep trap rewritten: an OU that is not registered gets no controls until you register the OU or enroll the account (control-tower-accounts-outside-not-bound); in a registered OU, preventive controls reach accounts 'under the OU, enrolled and unenrolled', but 'detective controls apply to enrolled accounts only' (control-tower-preventive-apply-unenrolled-detective-enrolled-only). The duplicate sentence in the Go deeper was removed.

findings.section: Question 8 (organizations-q008), Twin
findings.quote: **Twin.** If the stem said "teams create accounts with CreateAccount in a registered OU" instead: enroll those accounts and use Account Factory, because accounts created outside it [are not bound by the registered OU's controls].
findings.evidence: Fact control-tower-preventive-apply-unenrolled-detective-enrolled-only: 'When you enable controls on an organizational unit (OU) that is registered with AWS Control Tower, preventive controls apply to all member accounts under the OU, enrolled and unenrolled.' In the twin case the OU is registered, so the preventive controls already apply; what is missing is the detective controls ('detective controls apply to enrolled accounts only'). The twin teaches the reason that is wrong for exactly the case it describes. Fix the reason: 'because detective controls apply to enrolled accounts only; the preventive controls already apply'.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): q008 twin now: the preventive controls already reach accounts in a registered OU, but 'detective controls apply to enrolled accounts only', so enroll them (fact added to the question). The explanation now speaks of an OU that is not registered. Explanation and twin only; stem, options and key unchanged, so no new verification is needed.

findings.section: Predict (Predict 1) and its reveal in Check
findings.quote: **Predict 1.** A **service control policy** (SCP) on the root of an organization denies deleting log buckets. Can an administrator in the management account (the account that adds and pays for member accounts) still delete one? ... **Predict 1:** Yes: SCPs do not restrict [users or roles in the management account]
findings.evidence: Fact organizations-keep-resources-out-of-management-account (AWS recommends keeping resources out of the management account) and fact iam-scp-applies-to-member-root-user (an SCP 'restricts permissions for IAM users and roles in member accounts'). The prompt does not say where the log buckets are. The chapter's own design (log archive account, decision record figure 'logs in their own account') puts them in a member account; an administrator who reaches them from the management account works through a role in that member account, and the SCP applies. So 'Yes' is right only if the buckets sit in the management account. Fix: 'denies deleting log buckets. A log bucket sits in the management account. Can an administrator there still delete it?'
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): Predict 1 now says the bucket is stored in the management account; the reveal adds 'Member accounts stay protected.'

findings.section: Choose it or not (compare table, row 'Who builds a new account?')
findings.quote: | Who builds a new account? | Your team, for example with [AWS CloudFormation StackSets](../facts/organizations.md#organizations-stacksets-provision-to-accounts) |
findings.evidence: Fact organizations-stacksets-provision-to-accounts, source docs/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_introduction: 'programmatically creating new accounts using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), SDKs, or APIs, and centrally provision recommended resources and permissions to those accounts with AWS CloudFormation StackSets.' StackSets do not build accounts; they put a baseline into accounts that already exist. The skim gist 'StackSets build accounts' is wrong and shows up as a distractor pattern (Question 4 option 3). Fix: 'Your team: create accounts with the CLI or API, then deploy a baseline with AWS CloudFormation StackSets'.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): Row now: 'Your team: programmatically creating new accounts, then a baseline with AWS CloudFormation StackSets' (both links to organizations-stacksets-provision-to-accounts).

findings.section: A Control Tower landing zone ... (control type table)
findings.quote: | Proactive | [implemented using AWS CloudFormation hooks] | Checked [before the resources are provisioned] |
findings.evidence: Fact control-tower-proactive-only-cloudformation: 'Proactive controls check resources whenever those resources are created or updated by means of CloudFormation stack operations.' and 'these controls may not affect requests that are made directly to services through the AWS console, through AWS APIs'. READER: tables must give a correct gist on their own. From the table, Preventive is 'Stopped before it happens' and Proactive is 'Checked before ...': a skimmer sees two kinds of 'before' and concludes a proactive control also stops a CLI call. The CloudFormation-only scope appears only in the Stop-and-answer reveal. Fix the last cell: 'Checked when CloudFormation creates it; a console or CLI call is not checked'.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): Proactive cell now: 'Checked before the resources are provisioned, only by means of CloudFormation stack operations'.

findings.section: A Control Tower landing zone ... (Stop and answer)
findings.quote: Not reliably. Proactive controls check resources created [by means of CloudFormation stack operations].
findings.evidence: Fact control-tower-proactive-only-cloudformation ('may not affect requests that are made directly'). 'Not reliably' is a hedge she cannot use in an exam or in front of a customer. Fix: 'No, do not count on it: a proactive control checks only CloudFormation stack operations.'
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): Reveal now: 'No, do not count on it. A proactive control checks resources by means of CloudFormation stack operations.'

findings.section: A Control Tower landing zone ... (Why line)
findings.quote: Why keep controls that do not block? AWS says to use [preventive controls in combination with] detective controls.
findings.evidence: Fact control-tower-faq-complementary-to-security-hub, source AWS Control Tower FAQs: 'You should use the AWS Control Tower preventive controls in combination with the AWS Security Hub security best practice detective controls'. The quote is about Security Hub's detective controls, not Control Tower's, so the sentence claims more than its link (exemplar README mistake 1). It is also an appeal to authority, not a cause (exemplar thing 4: one 'Why' reason as a customer would hear it). Fix with a mechanism: 'A preventive control stops only the actions it lists. A detective control also finds what already exists or what came in another way, and reports it.' (ground any absolute word).
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): The 'Why keep controls that do not block?' sentence was removed (2-deep is at its 2,400-word ceiling). FAQ 4 keeps the complementary-services point with its verbatim FAQ quote.

findings.section: A Control Tower landing zone ... (step 2 and the audit-log line)
findings.quote: 2. **Create the shared accounts.** Next to the management account, it creates [the log archive account, and the audit account]. ... For the audit log, [member accounts can see the organization trail], but they cannot change or delete it.
findings.evidence: Fact organizations-log-archive-account-consolidates-logs (used by speak item organizations-s01 kp5) and fact organizations-org-trail-members-cannot-modify-or-delete ('a user in a management account can create an organization trail that logs all events for all AWS accounts in that organization'). The deep file never says what the log archive and audit accounts are for, and 'organization trail' appears once with no definition. Yet the chapter's spoken answer (s01, the exact question Chen asks in STARTUP.md) is built on the organization trail and the log archive account. She could not give that answer from the prose. Fix: one clause per shared account and one sentence defining the organization trail (created in the management account, logs every account).
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): Step 2 defines both shared accounts ('a repository for logs of API activities', 'a restricted account'); the audit-log line now starts 'an organization trail logs every account'.

findings.section: SCPs do not limit the management account or principals outside the organization (step 2 and table)
findings.quote: An RCP can affect [principals external to your organization]. ... | Question | SCP | RCP | Declarative policy |

findings.section: SCPs do not limit the management account or principals outside the organization (Exam trap)
findings.quote: > **Exam trap:** An SCP with an aws:PrincipalOrgID condition does not stop outsiders
findings.evidence: Rule: STYLE plain English and READER ('she forgets terminology'): aws:PrincipalOrgID is used nowhere else in the chapter prose and never explained, and Questions 7 and 9 hinge on aws:PrincipalOrgID and aws:ResourceOrgID. The belief the trap corrects is not one she would hold as written. Fix: one line per key ('aws:PrincipalOrgID: the caller's organization; aws:ResourceOrgID: the resource owner's organization') and phrase the trap as the belief: 'Wrong: an SCP can keep outsiders out of your buckets.'
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): Trap phrased as the belief ('Wrong: an SCP with aws:PrincipalOrgID keeps outsiders out of your buckets.'); the table row 'Key for the organization' explains aws:ResourceOrgID and aws:PrincipalOrgID.

findings.section: SCPs do not limit ... (Go deeper: the data perimeter)
findings.quote: SCPs and RCPs together build a [data perimeter around your identities and your resources].
findings.evidence: Fact organizations-scp-controls-which-resources-identities-access: 'SCPs provide an ability to control which resources your identities can access.' and 'RCPs provide an ability to control which identities can access your resources.' This direction rule is the whole of twin Questions 7 and 9 ('Your principals to outside resources: an SCP. Fix: put both quotes in the Go deeper with one example each (SCP with aws:ResourceOrgID; RCP with aws:PrincipalOrgID), or as a two-row table.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): The table now carries the direction rule with both verbatim displays (row 'Deciding question') and the keys (row 'Key for the organization'); the one-line Go deeper was removed.

findings.section: SCPs do not limit the management account or principals outside the organization (Stop and answer)

findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): q009 explanation now says 'preventive control' and links control-tower-control-types-mechanisms; 'guardrail' no longer appears.

findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): Trap now states the belief of its id (a partner company using your default subnets); the Go deeper defines participants ('the accounts that receive the shared subnets').

findings.section: Numbers that decide answers (B-list, Control Tower row) and FAQ 2
findings.quote: | [1000](../facts/control-tower.md#control-tower-ou-over-1000-accounts-cannot-register) | Accounts directly in an OU that Control Tower registers | ... No. China is the exception
findings.evidence: Fact control-tower-ou-over-1000-accounts-cannot-register: 'Existing OUs with over 1000 directly nested accounts cannot be registered or re-registered in AWS Control Tower.' The row reads as if Control Tower registers 1,000 accounts. Fix: 'Most accounts directly in an OU that Control Tower can register'. FAQ 2: 'China is the exception' suggests you pick a Region for China; the quote says you create a separate organization. Fix: 'No. For accounts used in China, create a separate organization.'
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): B-list row now 'Largest number of accounts directly in an OU that Control Tower registers'; FAQ 2 now 'No. Accounts used in China need a separate organization for accounts used in China.'

findings.section: How it works (depth check)
findings.quote: 3. **Inside principals.** SCPs limit member principals, ... and accounts [designated as delegated administrators].
